What win rate breaks even?
Break-even win rate is stop divided by stop plus target, before fees. Risk 14 to win 1 needs 93%, which is why an 81% win rate can still lose. Fees push it higher: a 0.5% stop at 1:1 needs 74% in crypto in our table.

Tested so you don't have to, part 2: RSI 30/70.

The rule: buy when the 14-day RSI falls below 30, sell when it rises above 70. We ran it on 40 US stocks from 2016-09-15 to 2025-03-14 (336 trades, 0.05% cost per side).

It made 7.4% a year. Holding the same 40 stocks made 18.0%. That is 10.5 points a year behind, and it was behind in both halves of the period (14.8 then 6.6 points a year). Its worst fall was 23.2% against 32.2% for holding, but it was in a position only 39.4% of the time. The p-value is 1.0, so there is no evidence it beats holding.

In-sample backtest, not a promise. The holding benchmark pays no costs.

The 95% interval for that average runs from -2.56 to +0.82 points, so it includes zero. A high win rate alone tells you nothing about whether a rule pays.

In-sample backtest, net of costs. A win is a trade that ends above zero after costs.
